name: Kao
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Tondo, Fanny Henry. 2020. The people of Kao and their language in the northern coast of Halmahera: a study of a Papuan language community in Austronesian world. Jurnal Masyarakat dan Budaya 22(2): 197-207. DOI 10.14203/jmb.v22i2.1074 (CC BY-SA 4.0).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Sociolinguistic/contact article; the only phonological remark is p. 203: 'Kao language phonologically consists of six vowels and nineteen consonants'. No word on stress, accent or syllables.

sources.citation: Retnowati, Endang (ed.). 2016. Identitas Bahasa dan Kebudayaan Etnik Minoritas Kao. Jakarta: LIPI Press. 252 pp. ISBN 978-979-799-778-6. Ch. 3 'Bahasa Kao di Desa Kao' by M. Umar Muslim, pp. 43 ff.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Chapter 3 section I 'Struktur bahasa Kao' (p. 58 ff.) covers only word order (SVO), pronominal agreement affixes and directionals; whole book a full-text search for stress/accent tekanan/aksen/stress/penult/suku kata/vokal/konsonan/fonem with no phonological hit. Book is anthropological/sociolinguistic (vitality, culture).

sources.citation: Voorhoeve, C. L. 1988. The languages of the North Halmaheran stock. In G. Smith et al. (eds.), Papers in New Guinea Linguistics No. 26, Pacific Linguistics A-76, pp. 181-209. Canberra: Pacific Linguistics. DOI 10.15144/PL-A76.181 (CC BY-SA 4.0).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Lexicostatistical classification and village lists; no phonological sketch of Kao. Only mention of Kao as a variety: p. 195, 'A special Kao dialect - according to Hueting a mixture of Ternate, Tobelo, Modole, and Pagu - may perhaps still be spoken in the township of Kao'.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page for Kao (kaoo1238) and its reference list.
sources.note: Glottolog lists no descriptive reference for Kao at all; only Wimbish 1991 (Pagu MA thesis, p. 6, 'comments on subclassification') and endangerment-status sources.
Nothing on phonology; its only sources are Retnowati 2016 (link used to download the LIPI book) and Ethnologue 2009.

sources.citation: Muslim, M. Umar. 2011/2012. Bahasa Kao di Desa Kao. Research report. Jakarta: PMB-LIPI.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Unpublished LIPI report underlying Muslim's chapter in Retnowati 2016; the report may contain the phonology the book chapter omits.

sources.citation: Wimbish, Sandra Gay. 1991. An introduction to Pagu through the analysis of narrative discourse. MA thesis, University of Texas at Arlington. 183 pp.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: online with a university library login
sources.note: Only Glottolog reference attached to Kao (p. 6 on subclassification); Pagu phonology sketch may state stress and how Kao relates to Pagu.

sources.citation: Perangin-Angin, Dalan Mehuli. 2018. A descriptive grammar of Pagu. PhD dissertation, Leiden University.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: open copy online, not downloaded; the linked copy was not accessible when a reader tried
sources.note: Modern grammar of Pagu, Kao's closest relative in the Kao River group (Kao has been treated as a Pagu-related or mixed dialect: Voorhoeve 1988 p. 195; Wimbish 1991 p. 6). Its phonology chapter gives Pagu stress and may comment on Kao; would be the fallback if Kao is subsumed under Pagu. Leiden repository could not be reached by automated download (connection reset).

sources.citation: Tondo, Fanny Henry. 2013. Kamus kecil Bahasa Kao. Jakarta: Pusat Penelitian Kemasyarakatan dan Kebudayaan (PMB-LIPI).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Only Kao-specific lexicographic work by a linguist who did 2013-2014 fieldwork; a dictionary front matter is the most likely place for a phoneme inventory and a stress note. Cited in Tondo 2020.

sources.citation: Budiman, Arif. 2012. Kamus pengantar Kao-Indonesia. Jakarta: PMB-LIPI.
